In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
androgen deprivation therapy prior to radical prostate surgery has no effect on the likelihood of a curative surgery.
the use of ADT before RP is not indicated in patients with clinically localized prostate cancer and that ADT prior to RP should be considered only in selected patients.
there is no evidence for or against the use of ADT prior to RP in patients with localized prostate cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the likelihood of curable radical prostatectomy is reduced in patients with T1 and T2 prostate cancers who receive androgen deprivation (AD) prior to radical prostatec- tomoy (RP), but that the likelihood of a positive surgical margin is not increased.
